subject: Career
title: The Exploding Offer Tactic
description: A fast breakdown of The Exploding Offer Tactic for builders.

hook.text: 'This offer expires Friday.' They're creating urgency to stop you from shopping around.

buildup.text: Exploding offers use time pressure to force decisions before you can compare alternatives.

discovery.text: Most 'deadlines' are soft. Politely asking for an extension often works without consequence.

twist.text: If they truly won't extend, that tells you how they treat employees — transactional from day one.

climax.text: Say: 'I want to give this the consideration it deserves. Can we extend to next Wednesday?'

punchline.text: Real deadlines are rare. Test them.

quiz.question: What should you do when given an exploding offer?

details.summary: An exploding offer is a job proposal with an artificially short deadline designed to pressure candidates into accepting before they can compare alternatives. Recognizing this tactic allows you to push back on unreasonable timelines without losing the opportunity.
details.whyItMatters: Companies use short deadlines because rushed candidates accept lower offers. Knowing the tactic exists lets you negotiate for reasonable decision time without panic.
takeaways: Exploding offers exploit urgency to prevent comparison shopping
Most employers extend deadlines when asked professionally
Any employer that refuses a reasonable extension is a warning sign

faq.question: How should I respond to an offer with only 48 hours to decide?
faq.answer: Express gratitude and enthusiasm, then professionally request an extension to one week. Explain that you want to give the decision the thoughtfulness it deserves. Most companies readily accommodate this because losing a candidate over two days is expensive.

faq.question: Are there situations where a short deadline is genuinely justified?
faq.answer: Yes. If the company has a hard start date tied to a project or training cohort, or if other finalists are waiting, a short timeline may reflect real constraints. Ask the employer to explain the urgency so you can evaluate legitimacy.
